newsitem.title: USA: Rexhall says Q4 hurt by losses in Indiana.
newsitem.headline: Rexhall says Q4 hurt by losses in Indiana.

text.p: Rexhall Industries Inc on Tuesday said its fourth quarter drop in net income was led by losses at the company's plant in Indiana.

"The Indiana facility...experienced an excess in labor costs coupled with buybacks and discounting which resulted in a loss," William Rex, chief executive officer, said in a statement. "This hurt our margins and overall performance."
Earlier Rexhall, a manufacturer of mobile homes and recreational vehicles, reported a share loss of $0.18 in the fourth quarter ended December 31 versus a profit of $0.17 per share one year ago.
Fourth quarter sales at Rexhall totaled about $13.7 million versus $14.6 million last year.
In a statement Rexhall said that it was disappointed by its fourth quarter loss but that the overall earnings pictures does not reflect positive results at its plant in California.
Rex said the company has transferred the manager at its California plant, Marco Martinez, to the Indiana unit.
"We are confident and look forward to positive results," Rex said.
